newsitem.title: UK: Dollar forges ahead, Eurobourses down.
newsitem.headline: Dollar forges ahead, Eurobourses down.

text.p: The dollar continued to forge ahead on Wednesday, breaking through important resistance barriers, while on the stock exchanges trading was lacklustre and leading shares were mostly lower.

After pausing for breath in early trading, the dollar extended a rally, sparked by central bank comments, against the mark and the yen which has seen it gain two pfennigs and a yen in value since last Friday's European close.
In Wednesday morning European trading it broke through the psychologically important 110 yen level for the first time since mid-July and overcame strong resistance at 1.5120 marks.
At 1100 GMT it was trading at 1.5122 marks and 110.30 yen.

Analysts said the underlying tone of the dollar remained positive amid speculation the U.S. Federal Reserve will raise interest rates later this month when its policy-making Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meets.

Comments by Federal Reserve Governor Janet Yellen on Tuesday added impetus to the dollar rally. Yellen suggested the U.S. economy looked vulnerable to inflation -- reinforcing the markets' feeling that there is an interest rate rise to come.
"The key question is how far the dollar can go, and it's beginning to look a bit overbought," said Nick Parsons, foreign exchange strategist at Banque Paribas in London.
"People are pondering whether it's a level to take profits, or to stick with the dollar for a move higher," he added.
On the bourses, London's leading shares were mixed in a listless market mid-morning with activity subdued and investors lacking any clear lead, dealers said.

A string of company results occupied attention first thing but trading swiftly settled into a sideways pattern. Wall Street provided little direction. It closed overnight 6.66 down at 5727.18 after adding 127 points over its previous two sessions.
Broadly in-line British earnings and jobs data left the market virtually unmoved and attention quickly shifted to New York in the hope of fresh impetus when Wall Street opened.

The unemployment rate fell to 7.5 percent in August, from 7.6 in July, after the number of jobless fell 15,600 to 2.11 million. The figures were in line with market expectations and the Treasury said they underlined strengthening economic activity.

On Tuesday the FTSE hit, but failed to maintain, a new intraday high of 3933.6. Traders said it could well challenge record territory again this week, with many still talking of 4,000 as a feasible short-term target.

In Frankfurt German shares continued to trade slightly lower at midday as dealers cited nervousness after the weaker overnight close of the Dow Jones Average while the continued strength of the dollar against the mark -- which makes German exports more attractive -- provided some support.

French shares also started weaker on consolidation, then came off their lows to move marginally into positive territory. "The market has been climbing for five days. It needs to breathe a bit," one trader said.
A big loser was carmaker Renault, down 7.82 percent after it reported late Tuesday a big slide in first-half profits.

On the precious metals market, palladium slid to its lowest fix in more than 33 months as speculators liquidated positions, dealers said. Palladium fixed at $123 an ounce, the lowest since December 29, 1993, and $1 lower than Tuesday afternoon.

A dealers said one reason has been steady selling from Russia, the world's largest producer, during the slack summer season when European industry was closed and demand was low. A major use of the rare metal is in automotive exhaust catalysts.
CURRENCIES AT 1100 GMT
The dollar was trading at 1.5122 marks and 110.30 yen compared with Tuesday's London close of 1.5087 marks and 109.80 yen.
STOCK MARKETS at 1100 GMT
The Financial Times-Stock Exchange index of 100 leading British shares had fallen 8.4 points to 3,907.7.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index was up 1.79 to 2,043.81.
The 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt was down 1.31 at 2,569.64.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold fixed at $383.15 against Tuesday's European close of 383.45. The market was very quiet and consolidating in the $382-$385 range.
